mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to increase borrowing and investment, thereby boosting equity prices and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive equity returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low UNRATE signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic strength and positive equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a positive HOUST signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, which is typically associated with positive equity returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a positive INDPRO signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and high retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer and business demand, which is typically associated with positive equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a positive GDPC1 and RSAFS signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals monetary tightening, which is typically associated with negative equity returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, which is typically associated with positive equity returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following a positive PAYEMS signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and high housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic activity, which is typically associated with positive equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a positive GDPC1 and HOUST signal, the hypothesis is rejected.
